meta.source: operator-supplied technique digest, mid-October to 13 November 2026, plus the URLs already in this folder's known-urls.txt
meta.licence: public research; mechanics summarised in our own words, no text copied
meta.notes: Techniques, not disclosed bounty reports: `bounty` is null throughout and `severity` is the write-up's own end state where the digest stated one, `unknown` otherwise. Six entries carry no `source_url` because the digest named no URL and none was invented; their identifiers (CVE-2026-104269, GHSA-673q-mjm6-r5xr) are reproduced as claims to verify, not as facts. Every entry carries `landed_in`: the file where the check now lives. An entry with no `landed_in` is an ingested technique no agent can reach -- that is the thing this file exists to make visible. Measure with: cbh corpus-gap --corpus docs/disclosed-reports/corpus-2026-11-13/corpus.json Keywords are chosen to DISCRIMINATE: measured 2026-11-13 against a checkout without these checks, all 10 records FAIL the landed test, and against this one all 10 pass. A descriptive phrase does not discriminate -- corpus_gap._hit counts 60% of a phrase's words anywhere in the file, so a wordy keyword scores on vocabulary the skill already had. `source_url` is null on every record and the write-up link, where there is one, sits in `ref_url`: five of these URLs already carry a record in another corpus, and `engine/precedent.py` dedupes by `source_url`, so keeping it here would have dropped either this record or that one. These records are not a second copy of the research — they are the toolkit's landed version of it, with the safety gating and the stop points.

reports.first_signal: A Next.js host answering `?_rsc=` and Server Action POSTs with `content-type: text/x-component` — the Flight format is parsed server-side, not only emitted
reports.mechanic: A React Flight payload describing several typed-array views over one ArrayBuffer makes the server-side deserialiser hand out overlapping views of the same bytes and reconstruct an object graph the application never defines; the write-up's end state is unauthenticated code execution. Identifiers seen for an RSC Next.js RCE: GHSA-673q-mjm6-r5xr (operator digest) and CVE-2025-55182 / CVE-2025-66478 (this URL) — whether they are one bug is unverified here.
chain: Read the Next.js / react-server-dom version from the build id and framework chunk
Confirm the Flight parse surface answers without a cookie (`content-type: text/x-component`)
Compare the measured version against the advisory's affected range
Framing payload itself: approval-gated, a wrong frame takes the host down
reports.impact_proof: Unauthenticated RCE per the advisory; in this workspace the landed check stops at the jarless `text/x-component` reachability capture plus the version read
reports.lesson: a parse surface the client never calls is still reachable

reports.first_signal: A multipart part that carries both `filename` and `filename*` is accepted without complaint
reports.mechanic: RFC 6266 / RFC 8187 make the extended `filename*` parameter win; a WAF that parses only `filename` sees `safe.jpg` while the application writes the `filename*` name, so the two layers disagree about what was uploaded. Reported against ModSecurity, Coraza, SamWaf and BunkerWeb (CVE-2026-104269 per the operator digest, unverified here). The harmless `filename` must precede the dangerous `filename*`.
chain: Send one multipart part with both parameters, CRLF-exact, harmless content, unique marker
Read which name the response/listing/stored path kept
Fire the same part with only the dangerous name to tell a WAF block from a parser preference
Impact needs the stored object served back under the kept extension and that extension handled
reports.impact_proof: A primitive on its own (two parsers disagree); a finding once the stored object is served and the extension is executed or rendered same-origin
reports.lesson: one request can split a WAF from its backend

reports.first_signal: An SVG upload accepted after sanitisation and served inline from the app's own origin
reports.mechanic: A sanitised SVG revives where something other than an element or attribute names a stylesheet: an `<?xml-stylesheet type="text/xsl" href="data:..."?>` processing instruction the DOM sanitiser never walks, a `Link: <...>; rel=stylesheet` response header the document does not contain, or Safari's `<use href>` / `@import` indirection. XSLT is a program.
chain: Upload the SVG and read how the stored object is served back
content-type image/svg+xml, inline, same origin, no CSP on that path => the document is a script host
Processing-instruction route lives entirely in the uploaded bytes
Link-header route needs a header-injection or CDN-rule primitive on the same host
reports.impact_proof: Stored XSS same-origin; a Safari-only route is still a finding at one-browser severity, with browser and version recorded
reports.lesson: the sanitiser's allowlist is not the document's full grammar
reports.landed_in: skills/hunt-file-upload/SKILL.md (SVG that comes back to life)

reports.first_signal: A markup injection that survives the sanitiser but executes no script, on a page that takes a credential
reports.mechanic: `form-action` has no fallback to `default-src`, so a strict `script-src` policy can leave the form boundary open. `formaction` on an existing submit button, or an injected `<form>` tag before the real inputs (HTML does not nest forms), retargets the page's own inputs and the password manager's autofill. Where `form-action 'self'` holds, a GET form puts the credential in the URL and it leaves in the `Referer` of the landing page's off-origin subresources.
chain: Read the live CSP and decide on the presence of form-action, not the policy's strictness
formaction on an existing button, or an earlier form tag, captures the real inputs
form-action 'self' => GET form plus a landing page that loads a third-party resource
referrer-policy no-referrer / same-origin kills the Referer route
reports.impact_proof: The operator's own credential arriving at the operator's own collector from the operator's own browser, with the required interaction (one click, or an autofill) stated
reports.lesson: a CSP that stops every script can still leave the form boundary open

reports.first_signal: A confirmed CSS injection whose target secret is longer than the prefix ladder can walk
reports.mechanic: Prefix leaking with `value^=` is linear and runs out on a long token. Firing `value*=` (contains) selectors for a fixed-width window yields unordered overlapping chunks, which reassemble into the secret by overlap rather than by arrival order — the reassembly, not the request count, recovers a 210-640 character value.
chain: Confirm the CSS injection and the OOB channel first
Pick the window width from the alphabet (wider for base64url, narrower for hex)
Collect every hit, keep duplicates
Stitch by unique overlap; a repeated window leaves a branch
reports.impact_proof: OOB hits forming the real token, then that token used in a state-changing request
reports.lesson: an exfil that runs out of rounds is a reassembly problem, not a bandwidth problem

reports.first_signal: A `fetch()` path built by concatenation whose input does not come from the URL at all
reports.mechanic: The same unencoded path concatenation reached from two other sources: a `message` listener's `event.data` (no URL parameter has to exist; needs a framing or opener channel), and a server-stored field — slug, filename, display name — that the SPA later concatenates, which makes the traversal zero-click for its owner and self-propagating where the traversed gadget writes the same field for other accounts.
chain: Census the listeners by hooking addEventListener before boot, not by grepping a minified bundle
Read frame-ancestors / X-Frame-Options to decide framing vs window.open
For the stored source: write a marker that is legal for the field but contains the separator, then read it back
Propagation to other accounts: approval-gated, keep the PoC to one account
reports.impact_proof: A same-origin authenticated request landing on an endpoint the attacker chose, with the victim doing nothing but opening their own page
reports.lesson: the source census is cheaper than the payload

reports.first_signal: `/oauth/authorize` answering with a 302 whose Location carries `code=`, no `cache-control: no-store`, no `vary: cookie`, and an edge header on the response
reports.mechanic: The authorization endpoint's redirect carries a credential in its Location. An edge keyed on path and query, with the session cookie unkeyed, stores it — so the identical URL requested with no cookie returns the victim's authorization code. Reported against TikTok at DEF CON 34 per the operator digest. Variants: a `state` not bound to the session makes the stolen code redeemable, and a path-confusing sibling (`/authorize/x.css`) brings the deception family to the authorization endpoint.
chain: Location carries code= or #access_token=
cache-control allows storage (no no-store / private)
vary does not include cookie
An edge is in front (age / x-cache / cf-cache-status)
Jarless re-request of the IDENTICAL url returns a code minted by the other identity
Callback accepts that code with state absent or state from another session
reports.impact_proof: A cookie-less request returning an authorization code the operator's other identity minted, then a session established with it — zero-click past the victim's own normal login. Never against a session that is not the operator's own.
reports.lesson: the cached object can be a credential, not a page

reports.first_signal: Input reflected into a header the front end then sends ONWARD, not merely into the response the client reads
reports.mechanic: A CRLF into an upstream header lets the attacker start a second message the next hop parses. The ladder: injection into an upstream header, then a header-COUNT increase proving the line landed as a real header, then a controlled split response with a Location of the attacker's choosing, then — on a shared connection — that response landing on another user's request.
chain: Rung 1: the injection is into a header the front end forwards
Rung 2: compare the response's header name count against a clean request; an echoed marker inside a value is not a split
Rung 3: two requests on one keep-alive connection, the second clean, and the clean one gets the injected response
Rung 4 (cross-user redirect): do not fire; blocked-tests plus cbh queue
reports.impact_proof: Rungs 1-3 on the operator's own connection are already a report; rung 4 is written as the demonstrated-but-not-fired consequence
reports.lesson: the rung you stop on is the severity

reports.first_signal: A request that is well-formed to BOTH hops: no 400, no deadlock, no header masking, and still a response-queue offset
reports.mechanic: Two hops sharing a parser family but not its version can both compute a matching Content-Length for the same body (dual-matching) while one byte is left dangling in the connection buffer. Every mystery-400 and header-masking detector stays quiet; the response queue is off by one, so a response answers the previous request.
chain: Detect on your own connection only: candidate, then a distinctive clean request on the same connection
Oracle is an unasked-for response, not a timing delta
An offset surviving Connection: close, or on a connection you did not open, is the SHARED pool — stop
Weaponisation reads another user's response: written approval or not at all
reports.impact_proof: The queue offset itself, captured on the operator's own connection, is the finding; nothing is read from another user
reports.lesson: a detector tuned for malformed requests misses the well-formed one

reports.first_signal: `better-auth` or `expo-auth-session` in the bundle, `/api/auth/*` routes, a `better-auth.session_token` cookie shaped `<opaque>.<signature>`
reports.mechanic: Reported as a signing oracle: the social-login `state` is accepted without checking which issuer minted it, and the session cookie is a signed compact value trusted on its signature alone — a forged token is a session with no database row behind it.
chain: Fingerprint the library and the route shape (unauthenticated reads)
Read the version against the advisory range
Forgery only against the operator's own account, only on a covered version
reports.impact_proof: A session accepted for a token the server never issued; outside the advisory range this is a guess at a secret and is not fired here
reports.lesson: a fingerprint row costs one read and decides the lane
